mechanism_narrative: Accelerating decline in WORKPLACES mobility (t-3w: -31.1% → t-0w: -45.6%) signals deepening workplace closures or remote-work mandates. This sustained contraction reduces commuting-linked retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined 14.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than the mean over the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES stabilizes or rebounds by week +2.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (t-3w: 18.1% → t-0w: 23.3%) combined with collapsing RETAIL_REC (-39.9% → -56.4%) indicates households are consolidating at home and deferring discretionary shopping. This behavioral shift persists, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while RETAIL_REC falls for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased 5.2 points while RETAIL_REC fell 16.5 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds above -40% in week +1 or RESIDENTIAL declines below 20% while RETAIL_REC rises.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility collapse (t-3w: -67.1% → t-0w: -75.6%) reflects public-transport restrictions or lockdown measures. Reduced transit access eliminates a primary route to retail districts, mechanically suppressing RETAIL_REC for the next four weeks regardless of demand.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -70% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -75.6% in t-0w, lowest of all categories
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -60% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not follow within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises despite TRANSIT remaining below -70%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapse (t-1w: -52.3% → t-0w: -43.3%) signals outdoor-activity restrictions are easing. This partial recovery in outdoor alternatives reduces substitution pressure on retail venues, but the lag between parks reopening and retail recovery is one week, so RETAIL_REC remains depressed in week +1 before rebounding in weeks +2–+4.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 9.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS continues to decline or remains flat over the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not rise above its four-week mean by week +4.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM decline (t-3w: -13.0% → t-0w: -24.1%) combined with RETAIL_REC collapse indicates households are reducing all discretionary mobility, including essential shopping. This signals demand destruction rather than substitution. If GROCERY_PHARM continues falling, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as consumer confidence erodes over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -20% while RETAIL_REC falls below -50%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell 11.1 points over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes or rises above -15% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not follow, or RETAIL_REC rises above -40% while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: August 15 marks mid-winter in Melbourne. Seasonal contraction in outdoor mobility (PARKS at -43.3%, TRANSIT at -75.6%) is compounded by policy restrictions. As spring approaches (late August–September), daylight hours and temperature improve, naturally lifting PARKS and TRANSIT mobility, which will drive RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2020-08-15, mid-winter in Southern Hemisphere
failure_condition: PARKS and TRANSIT do not both rise by more than 10 percentage points by week +4, or RETAIL_REC does not rise above its four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both in severe decline (WORKPLACES -45.6%, TRANSIT -75.6%), indicating coordinated lockdown or stage-4 restrictions. The interaction of workplace closure and transport shutdown eliminates commuting-linked retail trips. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed over the next week until restrictions ease; if both proxies remain below -60%, RETAIL_REC stays below -50%.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall below -60% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT at lowest levels in t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT rises above -50% within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -45% in week +1 while both proxies remain below -60%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen 5.2 percentage points over four weeks (18.1% → 23.3%) while all mobility categories collapsed, indicating a hard lockdown regime. This regime will persist for at least one more week based on the acceleration of restrictions (RETAIL_REC fell 16.5 points). RETAIL_REC will remain at or below -50% in week +1 before any policy reversal can take effect.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 20% while all other categories decline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 23.3% in t-0w, highest of all weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 20% within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -45% in week +1 despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 20%.
